newsitem.title: UK: Qatar Airways to launch daily London-Doha flights.
newsitem.headline: Qatar Airways to launch daily London-Doha flights.

text.p: Qatar Airways will begin daily London-Heathrow to Doha services on May 25 using Airbus Industrie A300-600s offering up to 10 tonnes of cargo capacity per flight, cargo manager John Curd told Reuters.
At present there are four flights a week.
From July 1, the airline will also manage its own cargo reservations, sales and accounts and cease using ANA Aviation Services as its general sales agent, he said in a telephone interview.
The change was due to Qatar Airways' growth and the promotion of "our own identity", and was not any reflection on ANA -- which has handled the carrier for the past three years -- Curd added.
Qatar Airways increased ex-UK air cargo rates by an average of eight percent from March 30 and yields have started to improve, he said.
A further rates rise is likely later this year, Curd added.

Apart from Doha itself, the carrier offers onward shipment to a number of cities including Bangkok, Manila, Colombo, Bombay, Trivandrum and Karachi as well as three new destinations -- Jeddah, Dharan and Kathmandu.
Rates to Bangkok and Manila are around 95 pence per kg for 100 kg and 80 pence to Bombay, he said.
There is also a weekly flight to Khartoum from Doha, while two destinations -- Dhaka and Madras -- have been dropped.

Inward business "is very heavy" and includes textiles as well as perishables from Colombo and other Far East centres. There are textile exports from Doha manufacturers as well as oil equipment being flown out for repairs, he said.
On May 6, the airline's senior general manager, Michael Hewitt, said in Dubai that it expected to see cargo account for 12 percent of total revenues this year against around seven percent in 1996.
He also said that it plans to take over operation of the Doha airport cargo terminal by early 1998. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
